questions.q: What does an Exact matching rule on a field require?
options: The values must be character-for-character identical (case-insensitive)
The values must share at least one common word
The values must be within a configurable similarity score
The values must both be non-blank, regardless of content
questions.explain: Exact matching requires identical values, case-insensitive. It's precise but misses near-matches like 'Acme Corp' vs. 'Acme Corporation.'

questions.q: Why would an admin add a Fuzzy field to a matching rule instead of relying on Exact alone?
options: Fuzzy matching runs faster than Exact matching
Fuzzy matching is required before a duplicate rule can reference the matching rule
Fuzzy fields are the only fields a duplicate rule can use
Fuzzy matching catches near-identical values Exact would miss, like abbreviations or punctuation differences
questions.explain: Fuzzy logic tolerates variation — abbreviations, word order, formatting — catching more real duplicates than an exact comparison would.

questions.q: In a custom matching rule, why is MatchBlank almost always left set to FALSE?
options: Setting it to TRUE disables the entire rule
Otherwise two records with an empty value in that field would be treated as a match
FALSE is required for Fuzzy fields, but not for Exact fields
It controls whether the rule applies to Leads versus Contacts
questions.explain: With MatchBlank = FALSE, blank values on both records don't count as a match. Leaving it TRUE would flag any two records that both happen to have an empty field.

questions.q: What is the relationship between a matching rule and a duplicate rule?
options: A matching rule and duplicate rule are the same configuration object under two names
A duplicate rule has its own comparison logic and ignores matching rules
A duplicate rule references one or more matching rules; the matching rule supplies the comparison logic
A matching rule can only be used by exactly one duplicate rule, ever
questions.explain: The duplicate rule points at a matching rule (or several, one per object it compares against) to decide what counts as a match, then applies its own action — block, alert, or report.

questions.q: An admin reports that a Contact duplicate rule is flagging many unrelated people as duplicates because it matches on fuzzy Last Name alone. What's the most direct fix?
options: Deactivate the matching rule entirely and rely on manual review
AND in a second field, such as fuzzy First Name or email, to narrow the match
Switch the field from Fuzzy to Exact without changing anything else
Change the duplicate rule's action from Block to Allow + Report
questions.explain: A single fuzzy field on a common value like a last name is too loose. Combining it with AND on a second field tightens the match without abandoning fuzzy logic altogether.
